section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the seventh rectification is called "And Truth" because its root is in the unchanging nature of G-d.
section.t: And one could say,
that this that the seventh rectification is called "And Truth"
(for the matter of truth is that which does not change)
is also because of its root,
for the level from which the drawing down of the seventh rectification comes is "I am G-d, I have not changed."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the highest level is drawn down to the lowest place, and that the true unchanging nature of G-d's Essence is drawn down primarily to the lower realm.
section.t: d)
And now, according to what is known,
that whatever is highest of the highest is drawn down to the lowest of the lowest,
it is understood
that the seventh rectification,
the rectification of "And Truth,"
is drawn down primarily to the lower realm.
And the explanation is,
that the true essence of the matter of "I am G-d, I have not changed" is in His Essence and Being, whose existence
is from His own Essence and is not caused by any cause that preceded Him, G-d forbid.
For in the revelations,
which are preceded by a cause and a reason,
one cannot say the true essence of the matter of "I have not changed,"
for this very thing—that they are preceded by a cause and a reason—
is itself a change,
for there is a change between before it was drawn from the cause and reason,
and at the time it is drawn from the cause and reason,
and after it is drawn from the cause and reason.
But regarding His Essence and Being, which is not caused by any cause that preceded Him, G-d forbid,
there is no change in Him, G-d forbid,
[and this is] the true essence of the matter of "I am G-d, I have not changed."
And this matter is drawn down primarily to the lower realm,
and as explained by the Mitteler Rebbe,
that this that the lower entity feels that its existence is from His Essence,
and in its feeling no cause or reason preceded it,
is because its root is from His Essence and Being, whose existence is from His own Essence and is not caused by any cause that preceded Him, G-d forbid,
for the true existence of the existence of the created being is true being.
And as is explained at length in the maamar "Mi Chamochah" of the Rebbe Maharash.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section notes that the maamar "Mi Chamochah" was one of the Rebbe Maharash's fixed discourses, repeated every few years.
section.t: [For,
as revealed by my father-in-law, the Rebbe,
— each of the Rebbes had fixed discourses which they would repeat publicly once every two or three years,
and one of these discourses of the Rebbe Maharash was the maamar "Mi Chamochah"],
